prompt.context: Your client is a national burrito chain with 100 locations. There has been a widespread flu virus growing in the U.S. which has the potential to hurt their business. They need your help deciding how they should respond to the virus in NYC specifically, and what the implications will be for their brand.
prompt.question: How should the client respond to the virus in NYC, and what will the financial and brand implications be?

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does the client have in NYC?

clarifying_info.a: The restaurants sell 3 types of burritos, along with guacamole, salsa, and other sides.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current service model?
clarifying_info.a: All sales come from grab-and-go takeout orders. Tres Burritos does not currently offer delivery.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's primary goal?
clarifying_info.a: Their main goal is maintaining a net positive profit. They are also concerned about how their actions in NY will affect the national brand.

clarifying_info.q: How long is the virus expected to last?
clarifying_info.a: The virus is projected to last for 3 months.

clarifying_info.q: How is Tres Burritos responding in other cities?
clarifying_info.a: We do not know how Tres Burritos is responding in other cities.

exhibits.title: Income Statement — Monthly (per restaurant)
exhibits.shows: A monthly per-restaurant income statement listing revenue, individual expense line items, and EBITDA.

exhibits.title: Tres Burritos NYC Customers' Place of Residence
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing the breakdown of NYC customer residence by geography across four segments.

exhibits.title: Tres Burritos Restaurant Footprint (as of June 2020)
exhibits.shows: A map or chart showing the number of Tres Burritos locations across different cities or regions.

framework: Identify options for responding to the virus: Stay Open, Close, or Modify (delivery, curbside, partial closure, changed hours, close some stores)
Evaluate profitability of each option: analyze impact on Revenue (product mix, # orders, avg check) and Costs (fixed: rent, equipment, SG&A, marketing; variable: labor, COGS)
Assess external considerations: virus duration/spread/location, competitor actions, NYC population behavior, national brand impact

questions.prompt: How would you evaluate the options for responding to the virus?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify at least three distinct options beyond a binary open/close decision. A pro/con matrix or structured comparison is acceptable. Candidate should conclude by requesting profitability data to evaluate financial impact of each option.

questions.prompt: Governor Hamilton has decided restaurants can only offer delivery. What will the virus's impact be on Tres Burritos' profitability per location over the 3-month period?
questions.guidance: Candidate should use Exhibit 1 as the baseline and apply the stated changes. Key insight: the $20,000 delivery setup cost is one-time (Month 1 only), so profitability differs between Month 1 and Months 2-3. Candidate should recognize the 3-month horizon and calculate total EBITDA across all months. Takeaway: EBITDA is negative in Month 1 but positive over the full 3 months, making delivery better than closing entirely.

math.setup: Baseline: Revenue $100K, COGS $10K, Wages+SG&A+Overhead (fixed) $60K, EBITDA $30K. Changes: Revenue -10%, COGS +10%, one-time delivery setup cost $20K in Month 1.
steps: Decline from baseline 3-month EBITDA of $90,000: ~60% decline
Bonus: 10 NYC locations x $37,000 = $370,000 total NYC EBITDA
math.answer: $37,000 EBITDA per location over 3 months (~60% decline vs. baseline $90,000); $370,000 total across all 10 NYC locations.

questions.prompt: What are some possible ways to improve EBITDA if they choose to keep restaurants open and offer delivery?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm both revenue-increase and cost-reduction levers. Strong answers go beyond the obvious and show creativity around the pandemic context.

brainstorming.prompt: What are some possible ways to improve EBITDA if they choose to keep restaurants open and offer delivery?

categories.name: Increase Revenue
ideas: Offer groceries — sell raw ingredients directly from the kitchen to customers
Partner with other local restaurants to drive cross-traffic
Raise prices to offset lower volume
Increase presence on third-party delivery apps (Seamless, etc.) to capture more orders

categories.name: Decrease Costs
ideas: Reduce staff to lower wage costs
Close some of the 10 NYC stores to eliminate fixed overhead on underperforming locations
Limit menu options to reduce ingredient complexity and COGS
Reduce the $20K delivery setup cost by launching via an existing third-party service (Seamless, Caviar) instead of building own delivery infrastructure

recommendation: Offer delivery across the 10 NYC locations to generate $37,000 EBITDA per location ($370,000 total) over the 3-month virus period, versus zero or negative EBITDA from closing stores entirely.
Although EBITDA will decline ~60% from baseline, this option preserves positive total profitability and maintains customer relationships.
risks: Revenues decline more than the projected 10%
Customers migrate to competitors during the virus period and do not return afterward
Risk of spreading disease through food handling or delivery personnel
A problem with the delivery launch could damage the national brand
next_steps: Find a delivery partner and plan logistics to launch (consider Seamless or Caviar to reduce the $20K setup cost)
Explore additional cost reductions (staff optimization, menu simplification, possible store consolidation)
Monitor what Tres Burritos and competitors are doing in other cities to align national strategy
